en: It's for me; Third person present of ser marking identity or an inherent trait.
Is he here?; Third person present of estar for location or a passing state.
I'm fine; I-form present of estar for a state or a place.
He still hasn't; Third person present of haber used as auxiliary before a past participle.
Let's go already!; We-form present of ir also used as let's go.
Is there anything?; Third person present of haber used impersonally for there is or there are.
I don't have anything; I-form present of tener meaning to have or hold.
How are you?; You-singular present of estar for a state or a place.
I don't know why; I-form present of saber meaning to know a fact.
I already have; I-form present of haber used as auxiliary before a past participle.
It has to be me; Infinitive ser for identity and inherent qualities.
He has something of mine; Third person present of tener meaning to have or hold.
I can't take any more; I-form present of poder meaning to be able or allowed.
I don't want anything else; I-form present of querer meaning to want or to love a person.
I don't know what to do; Infinitive hacer meaning to do or to make.
It was all because of you; Third person preterite of ser for one finished past occasion.
Thanks for everything; Feminine plural noun for thanks from gracia which alone means grace or wit.
Not again; Feminine noun for a time or occasion with plural veces.
He used to be like that; Third person imperfect of ser for how something used to be.
I'm not like that; I-form present of ser for my identity or lasting traits.
Are they for me?; They-form present of ser for identity or inherent traits of several.
What have you got there?; You-singular present of tener meaning to have or hold.
I think so; I-form present of creer meaning to believe or think something.
I'm on my way there now; I-form present of ir meaning to go or to be heading somewhere.
Do you know anything about him?; You-singular present of saber meaning to know facts or information.
It was here earlier; Third person imperfect of estar for an ongoing past state.
Could that be?; Third person present of poder and puede ser means maybe.
You're just like that; You-singular present of ser for identity and lasting character.
That isn't true; Feminine noun for truth and as ¿verdad? it tags a sentence.
Let's go to my place; Feminine noun for house or home taking no article in en casa.
I don't have time; Masculine noun for time and also for the weather.
How's everything going?; Third person present of ir meaning goes or is going.
Please don't; Masculine noun for a favour fixed in the request por favor.
What do you want from me?; You-singular present of querer meaning to want or to love someone.
I'm very sorry; I-form present of sentir meaning to feel and lo siento apologises.
Is the gentleman here?; Masculine noun for a gentleman or sir or Mr before a surname.
A long time ago; Third person present of hacer and with a time span means ago.
You have to do something; You-singular present of haber used as auxiliary before a past participle.
What do you mean?; Infinitive decir meaning to say or to tell.
We have to do something; We-form present of tener and tener que means to have to.
Where is everybody?; They-form present of estar for their location or current state.
Can you do that?; You-singular present of poder meaning to be able or allowed.
I can't see anything; Infinitive ver meaning to see.
Oh come on!; Masculine noun for a man and in Spain an exclamation of appeal.
That's life; Feminine noun for life and mi vida is an endearment.
There are lots of things; Feminine plural noun for things from singular cosa.
I have to go; Infinitive ir meaning to go and ir a plus infinitive is future.
I'm ten years old; Masculine plural noun for years used with tener for age.
I want to be here; Infinitive estar for a state or a place.
All day; Masculine noun for a day and masculine despite its final a.
I can't tonight; Feminine noun for night or evening with esta noche meaning tonight.
We're here now; We-form present of estar for location and temporary states.
I agree with you; Masculine noun for an agreement used in the phrase estar de acuerdo.
I don't have a job; Masculine noun for work or a job.
Sounds good to me; Third person present of parecer to seem or to look like.
There are a lot of people here; Feminine noun for people though grammatically singular so it takes a singular verb.
Whatever works is fine; Third person present subjunctive of ser with lo que sea meaning whatever.
My father isn't in; Masculine noun for father whose plural padres usually means parents.
Look at this; You-singular command of mirar to look at or watch.
Who said that?; Third person preterite of decir to say or tell.
What do you want?; Third person present of querer to want or to love a person.
It could be; First or third person conditional of poder meaning could or might.
I want to talk to you; Infinitive of hablar to speak or talk.
Where are you going?; You-singular present of ir with vas a plus infinitive as the future.
What's going on?; Third person present of pasar to happen or pass or spend time.
They have to talk to me; They-form present of haber the auxiliary for perfect tenses like han hablado.
Do you have any money?; Masculine noun for money and uncountable so it has no plural.
I want to see the world; Masculine noun for world with todo el mundo meaning everybody.
One moment please; Masculine noun for a moment with en este momento meaning right now.
Can I have one?; Infinitive of tener to have or hold with tener que meaning to have to.
I have been here; Past participle of estar used after haber and invariable.
There were a lot of people; Third person imperfect of haber meaning there was or there were always singular.
He didn't have any money; First or third person imperfect of tener for ongoing past possession.
And your mother?; Feminine noun for mother though mamá is the usual term of address.
Okay see you tomorrow; Third person present of valer to be worth also Spain's everyday okay.
What place is this?; Masculine noun for a place with tener lugar meaning to take place.
What are you doing?; Gerund of hacer used with estar for doing or making right now.
Nobody knows anything; Third person present of saber to know a fact or how to do something.
We can go tomorrow; We-form present of poder to be able or may.
Hold on a second; You-singular command of esperar to wait or hope.
What became of him?; Past participle of ser invariable after haber for has been.
That's something else; Feminine noun for a thing with la cosa es que meaning the thing is.
How is your son?; Masculine noun for son whose plural hijos covers children of either sex.
What kind of man?; Masculine noun for a type or kind and informally a guy.
Are you his friend?; Masculine noun for a male friend with no romantic meaning.
Who is that woman?; Feminine noun for woman and also wife as in mi mujer.
Mom I'm coming; Feminine noun for mom the affectionate everyday word for one's mother.
Is dad home?; Masculine noun for dad the affectionate everyday word for one's father.
Three days ago; Masculine plural of día meaning days as in buenos días.
What does she say?; Third person present of decir to say with dice que reporting speech.
I need to talk to you; First person present of necesitar to need something.
I didn't say that; First person preterite of decir for what I said.
Hey have you got a minute?; You-singular command of oír also used to grab attention.
I like this place; Third person present of gustar to be pleasing so the liked thing is subject.
I just wanted to see you; First or third person imperfect of querer for wanting or a softened request.
Can it be true?; Third person future of ser also used to guess that something probably is.
There might be something; Infinitive of haber giving there is after another verb as in puede haber.
Somewhere else; Feminine noun for a part with en alguna parte meaning somewhere.
What's your name?; Masculine noun for a name with a nombre de meaning in the name of.
What a mess!; Feminine noun for shit genuinely vulgar and used alone as a curse.
That must be true; Third person present of deber, must or ought to before an infinitive.
I haven't seen anything; Irregular past participle of ver, invariable after haber.
I don't care at all; Third person present of importar, to matter or be of concern.
They have a lot of money; They-form present of tener, to have or hold.
We've seen everything; We-form present of haber, the auxiliary for have done something.
You're right; Feminine noun meaning reason, tener razón is to be right.
I want to know the truth; Infinitive saber, to know facts or information.
Who did this?; Third person preterite of hacer, did or made.
Sometimes I don't know; Feminine plural of vez, times or occasions as in a veces.
They don't see anything; They-form present of ver, to see.
I have no idea; Feminine noun for an idea, ni idea means no clue.
There's a problem; Masculine noun for a problem despite the final a.
What time is it?; Feminine noun for a clock hour or an appointment slot.
Love of my life; Masculine noun for love, mi amor is a common endearment.
He doesn't see well; Third person present of ver, to see.
My whole family is here; Feminine noun for family, grammatically singular so it takes a singular verb.
The police are here; Feminine noun where la policía is the force and un policía one officer.
I should go; First person conditional of deber, should or ought to.
That girl doesn't like me; Feminine noun for a girl or a young woman.
Let's go guys!; Masculine plural of chico, guys or kids including a mixed group.
He tells me everything; Third person present of contar, to tell or to count.
What are you doing here?; You-singular present of hacer, to do or to make.
I want to get out of here; Infinitive salir, to leave or go out of a place.
What a problem!; Third person present subjunctive of ir, also an exclamation meaning wow.
See you tomorrow; I-form present of ver, to see.
They're my friends; Masculine plural of amigo, friends including women in a mixed group.
My brother is a police officer; Masculine noun for brother, the plural hermanos means siblings.
I thought he was my friend; I-form preterite of pensar, thought or believed.
I didn't know anything about this; First person imperfect of saber, knew or used to know.
I've got something in my head; Feminine noun for the head, also where ideas and sense sit.
Thanks sweetheart; Masculine noun for affection, also a term of endearment for anyone.
What do I say now?; I-form present of decir, to say or to tell.
Where are you all going?; They-form present of ir, to go.
Two men are here; Masculine plural of hombre, men or an interjection expressing surprise.
We're friends; We-form present of ser, marks identity or an inherent trait.
That's no way to talk; Feminine noun for a shape or a way of doing something.
He's next to me; Masculine noun for a side, al lado de means beside.
I have to talk to you; I-form present of deber, must or with an object to owe.
It would be a problem; Third person conditional of ser, would be.
In that case I'm not going; Masculine noun for a case, hacer caso means to pay attention.
You can go out; They-form present of poder, can or be allowed to.
What happened?; Third person preterite of pasar, happened or passed by.
That boy is my brother; Masculine noun for a boy or a young guy, also means small.
I didn't do anything; I-form preterite of hacer, did or made.
There are a lot of people here; Feminine plural of persona, individual people you can count.
Is the lady of the house in?; Feminine noun for a married or older woman, also means wife.
I want to go back home; Infinitive volver, to return or with a plus infinitive to do again.
Let's go along that path; Masculine noun for a road or path, en camino means on the way.
He's talking to my mother; Gerund of hablar, talking and also used after seguir or ir.
No way; Feminine noun for a way or a method, de ninguna manera means no way.
Who is that person?; Feminine noun for a person and always feminine even about a man.
I need your help; Feminine noun for help and alone it is a shout for help.
Do you know this story?; Feminine noun covering both a story and history.
I was going to say something; Imperfect of ir used for I or he was going.
I suppose so; First person present of suponer meaning to suppose or assume.
I do not understand anything; First person present of entender meaning to understand.
Someone is at the door; Feminine noun for a door or a gate.
Do you see what I mean?; You-singular present of ver meaning to see.
Nothing is going to happen; Infinitive pasar meaning to happen or pass by or spend time.
What does that mean?; Third person present of significar meaning to mean.
What day of the week is it?; Feminine noun for a week and fin de semana is the weekend.
I hope to see you today; First person present of esperar meaning to hope or wait or expect.
One more year here; Masculine noun for a year.
The kids are not here; Masculine plural of niño for children including mixed groups of boys and girls.
Hey man! What are you doing?; Masculine noun for an uncle and in Spain a casual dude.
You are so lucky!; Feminine noun for luck which you have with tener suerte.
We are going to another city; Feminine noun for a city with the plural ciudades.
He does not even know my name; Adverb paired with ni to mean not even.
Do you want to come with me?; Infinitive venir meaning to come toward the speaker.
My daughter is two years old; Feminine noun for a daughter.
I would like to talk with you; Third person conditional of gustar meaning it would please me.
Wait five minutes; Masculine plural of minuto for minutes.
His father's death; Feminine noun for death despite the final -e.
Can you leave that here?; Infinitive dejar meaning to leave something or let someone do something.
Actually I do not know; Feminine noun for reality and en realidad means actually.
He does not stop talking; Third person present of dejar and dejar de means stop doing something.
We have problems; Masculine plural of problema and masculine despite the final -a.
Nobody gives me anything; Third person present of dar meaning to give.
My heart is yours; Masculine noun for a heart with the plural corazones.
I am scared; Masculine noun for fear which you have with tener miedo.
Where is the boss?; Masculine noun for a boss with la jefa for a woman.
I want a little water; Feminine noun for water though it takes el in the singular.
I have been waiting three hours; Feminine plural of hora for hours or clock time.
Power is everything; Masculine noun for power from the infinitive of the same form.
My wife is at home; Feminine noun for a wife and in the plural also handcuffs.
Hands up!; Feminine plural of mano for hands and feminine despite the final -o.
You must see this; You-singular present of deber meaning must or ought to.
Is anyone else coming?; Third person present of venir meaning to come toward the speaker.
Come on! Let's go!; Third person present subjunctive of venir also the usted command.
She has her mother's eyes; Masculine plural of ojo for eyes and ¡Ojo! warns you to watch out.
I want to find a place; Infinitive encontrar meaning to find with the stem change in encuentro.
Give me your hand; Feminine noun for a hand and feminine despite the final -o.
That boy is my son; Masculine noun for a small boy or child.
I do not want to see your face; Feminine noun for a face.
Careful with the water!; Masculine noun for care used in tener cuidado to be careful.
Three nights without you; Feminine plural of noche for nights as in buenas noches.
It is the end of the world; Masculine noun for an end and por fin means at last.
Shall we go for a drink?; Infinitive tomar meaning to take or to drink.
Listen to your mother; Third person present of escuchar and also the tú command.
We are about to leave; Masculine noun for a point or dot or full stop.
Is he still here?; Third person present of seguir meaning to follow or to keep on being something.
I hope there is water; Third person present subjunctive of haber used after words that demand that mood.
My team is my family; Masculine noun for a team or the gear and kit for a job.
Your father needs help; Third person present of necesitar meaning to need something.
What time are you going to arrive?; Infinitive of llegar meaning to arrive and it takes a before the destination.
The doctor is already here; Masculine noun for a doctor and also a title of address.
If only there were time; Third person past subjunctive of haber used for unreal wishes and if-clauses.
My car is at home; Masculine noun for a car and the everyday word in Spain.
What do I do now?; First person present of hacer meaning to do or make.
I have class in the morning; Feminine noun for a class or lesson and also a kind or sort.
Why do you say that?; You-singular present of decir meaning to say or tell.
What is your mother's name?; Third person present of llamar meaning to call and with se to be named.
Take my hand; Third person present of tomar meaning to take or drink and also a command.
The earth is our home; Feminine noun for soil or land or the planet itself.
This war has no end; Feminine noun for war and dar guerra is the idiom for being a handful.
Let me think for a moment; Infinitive of pensar meaning to think and pensar en is to think about something.
I hope she can come; Third person present subjunctive of poder meaning to be able to do something.
There is blood in the water; Feminine noun for blood with no ordinary plural.
The women are here already; Plural of the feminine noun mujer meaning women and also wives.
Just one more lap; Feminine noun for a turn or a lap or the change from a payment.
It was me; First person preterite of ser meaning it was me and shared with ir.
I don't want to work today; Infinitive of trabajar meaning to work with trabajar en naming the workplace.
I haven't had time; Past participle of tener used with haber and never changing for gender.
I like this game; Masculine noun for a game or a match and also a set of things.
His body isn't well; Masculine noun for a body and also a corps of people.
Can I come in?; Infinitive of entrar meaning to go in taking en or a before the place.
Nobody believes me; Third person present of creer meaning to believe and creer en is to believe in.
She couldn't speak; Third person imperfect of poder painting an ongoing inability rather than one failed moment.
We have to go now; We-form present of deber meaning must and deber plus infinitive is obligation.
Give me a chance; Feminine noun for a chance or an opening for something.
Where is my phone?; Masculine noun for a telephone and por teléfono means on the phone.
We need more time; We-form present of necesitar meaning to need and it takes its object directly.
In the end nothing happened; Masculine noun for an ending while la final is a championship match.
Are you going to the party?; Feminine noun for a party and also a public holiday.
Where were you last night?; You-singular imperfect of estar the normal past for location and states.
Everybody wants money; Third person plural present of querer meaning to want and with a to love.
My brother's car; Masculine noun for a car short for automóvil and usual in Latin America.
Can you give me something?; Infinitive of dar meaning to give and it builds idioms like dar miedo.
I want to live here; Infinitive of vivir meaning to live with vivir de naming what you live on.
My sister knows nothing; Feminine noun for a sister while the plural hermanos covers mixed siblings.
What's your number?; Masculine noun for a number and also a size or an issue.
Just two more months; Plural of the masculine noun mes meaning months and el mes que viene is next month.
It's not my fault; Feminine noun for fault or blame and tener la culpa is to be guilty.
The kids are at school; Feminine noun for a school usually the primary one.
He has already left; Past participle of ir and with se it means having left.
What are you saying?; Gerund of decir used with estar to build the progressive.
Your boss talks a lot; Third person present of hablar meaning to speak or talk to someone.
Maybe it's in the car; Third person present subjunctive of estar used after words of doubt like quizás.
I have a question; Feminine noun for a question and you hacer una pregunta rather than say one.
The girls are talking; Plural of the feminine noun chica meaning girls or young women.
Were they your friends?; Third person plural imperfect of ser, how people or things used to be.
What's going on?; Gerund of pasar, to happen or to pass by or to spend time.
Where is the captain?; Masculine noun for a captain, a ship's master or a team leader.
My sister has a baby; Masculine noun for a baby, it stays masculine even for a girl.
We don't know anything; We-form present of saber, to know facts or information.
Do you like the food?; Feminine noun for food and also the main meal of the day.
I don't want to die; Infinitive morir, to die, the stem becomes ue in muero.
I don't know that man; I-form present of conocer, to know or be acquainted with people.
Shall we go eat something?; Infinitive of comer, to eat and often to have lunch.
A wine please; Masculine noun for wine, the drink made from grapes.
Do you have the list?; Feminine noun for a list, as an adjective it means ready or clever.
I want him to do it; Third person present subjunctive of hacer, to do or make, required after querer que.
I have two children; Masculine plural of hijo, sons or children of both sexes.
My parents are here; Masculine plural of padre, usually the two parents together.
The room is ready; Feminine noun for a room, a bedroom or a hotel room.
I can't believe this; Infinitive of creer, to believe or to think something true.
I'm thinking about you; Gerund of pensar, to think, pensar en means to think about.
It was two days; Third person plural preterite of ser, a finished fact about identity.
What's it about?; Third person present of tratar, to treat, tratarse de means to be about.
I'm looking for you; Gerund of buscar, to look for, it takes no preposition.
I was never afraid; I-form preterite of tener, to have, a completed past state.
I love you so much; I-form present of amar, to love deeply.
You're very young; Adjective meaning young, also a noun for a young person of either sex.
A couple of hours; Masculine noun for a pair, un par de means a couple of.
What are they doing here?; Third person plural present of hacer, to do or make.
We'll keep going like this; Infinitive of seguir, to follow or to keep doing something.
What do they say?; Third person plural present of decir, to say or tell.
I haven't got a clue; Feminine noun for a whore, most often a very crude intensifier.
They don't know anything; Third person plural present of saber, to know facts or information.
It doesn't make sense; Masculine noun for meaning or sense and also a direction of travel.
Don't do that; You-singular subjunctive of hacer, used for the negative command don't do.
We have to wait a bit; Infinitive of esperar, to wait or to hope or to expect.
He has a weapon; Feminine noun for a weapon, it takes el in the singular.
That's five dollars; Masculine plural of dólar, dollars as money.
They were at the house; Third person plural imperfect of estar, a past place or state.
It's for your safety; Feminine noun for safety and security and also confidence.
He was here yesterday; Third person preterite of estar, a finished stay somewhere.
Don't worry; You-singular subjunctive of preocupar, no te preocupes means don't worry.
Give me your word; Feminine noun for a word and also a promise you give.
We're waiting for you; Gerund of esperar, to wait for or to expect.
There's nothing left; Third person present of quedar, to remain or be left.
Is he in his office?; Feminine noun for an office or a public bureau.
You can't kill anyone; Infinitive of matar, to kill, the victim needs a personal a.
I'll go with you; I-form future of ir, I will go.
The baby is in bed; Feminine noun for a bed as in irse a la cama.
I haven't heard anything; Past participle of oír, to hear, also the noun for ear.
There wouldn't be any problems; Third person conditional of haber, there would be or would have.
Where can my phone be?; Third person future of estar, often a guess about the present.
He gave me his number; Third person preterite of dar, to give.
It's a keepsake from my father; Masculine noun for a memory or a souvenir, recuerdos also sends regards.
He is not being fair; Gerund of ser used with estar for temporary behaviour rather than fixed identity.
I hope he is right; Third person present subjunctive of tener and also the polite usted command.
There is no light here; Feminine noun for light or daylight or electricity with plural luces.
What the hell is he doing?; Plural of the masculine demonio used as a mild swear after qué.
I want to sleep a bit; Infinitive of dormir meaning to sleep and stem-changing to duermo.
This is not his place; Masculine noun for a spot or seat and un sitio web means website.
Can I help with something?; Infinitive meaning to help and it takes a personal a before people.
I have to get hold of some money; Infinitive meaning to obtain or manage after effort with yo form consigo.
My husband knows nothing; Masculine noun for husband and the everyday word in speech.
Leave me alone; Feminine noun for peace and en paz means left alone.
I do not like your plan; Masculine noun for a plan with plural planes.
He has given me his word; Past participle of dar meaning given and invariable after haber.
His father died yesterday; Third person preterite of morir meaning he or she died.
The whole village knows; Masculine noun for a village or a people as a nation.
Has anyone come?; Past participle of venir meaning come toward the speaker.
Enough problems already!; Third person present of bastar used impersonally to mean that is enough.
One step at a time; Masculine noun for a step or pace.
We should talk about this; We-form conditional of deber and a polite way to suggest something.
I like this music; Feminine noun for music and also sheet music or a band's sound.
I want him to tell the truth; Third person present subjunctive of decir and also the usted command.
Hold on a minute; Masculine noun for minute and often just a moment in speech.
I am going to call the police; Infinitive meaning to call by phone or by shouting or by name.
Nobody thinks about me; Third person present of pensar meaning thinks with pensar en for about.
It is not my country; Masculine noun for country with plural países.
I am the king of the world; Masculine noun for king with plural reyes covering the Three Wise Men.
Sorry about yesterday; Masculine noun for a standalone apology or a request to get past.
More time is needed; Feminine noun for a lack and hacer falta means to be needed.
I think about you always; First person present of pensar meaning I think.
Where the hell were you?; Plural of the masculine diablo used as a mild intensifier after questions.
I have lost my job; Past participle of perder meaning lost or missed.
That girl is my daughter; Feminine noun for a girl of roughly under twelve.
Are you all right miss?; Feminine title for a young woman and now dated as address.
He has been waiting two hours; Third person present of llevar which with a time span means has been.
He is in hospital; Masculine noun for hospital with plural hospitales and it keeps the article.
Somebody has called you; Past participle of llamar meaning called or named.
What do we do now?; We-form present of hacer and also used as let us do.
Can you take me home?; Infinitive meaning to take or carry something away from here.
Got a light?; Masculine noun for fire and asking for fuego requests a light.
It was his fault; Third person preterite of tener and tener la culpa means to be blamed.
I am going to put some music on; Infinitive meaning to put or place with yo form pongo.
There are people in the street; Feminine noun for street and en la calle can mean outdoors.
He has just left; Third person present of acabar and acabar de means to have just.
It is the proof I need; Feminine noun for proof or a test or a rehearsal or fitting.
This book is mine; Masculine noun for a book.
Everything is in order; Masculine el orden means sequence while feminine la orden is a command.
He was here for two weeks; Plural of the feminine semana meaning weeks.
Do you want a coffee?; Masculine noun for coffee and for the cafe with plural cafés.
We are going to start now; Infinitive meaning to begin with yo form empiezo and empezar a plus infinitive.
We want to talk with you; We-form present of querer meaning we want or we love.
Whose dog is this?; Masculine noun for dog with feminine perra.
Look at the sky; Masculine noun for the sky and also for heaven.
What is your position?; Masculine noun for a job post or a market stall.
How was the trip?; Masculine noun for a trip or journey.
What would he do?; Third person conditional of hacer meaning would do or would make.
Do not ask any more questions; Feminine plural of pregunta for questions which you hacer rather than say.
What do you think?; You-singular present of pensar meaning to think or hold an opinion.
I have always loved you; Past participle of querer meaning loved or wanted and also dear.
I am going to get help; Infinitive meaning to look for or fetch with no preposition after it.
I will not tell you anything; First person future of decir meaning I will say or tell.
That sounds good; Third person present of sonar meaning to sound or to ring.
Do you want to play with me?; Infinitive meaning to play a game or a sport.
I need change for the coffee; Masculine noun for a change or the coins from a payment.
Let us watch a movie; Feminine noun for a movie or a roll of film.
That is worth millions; Masculine plural of millón meaning millions and taking de before a noun.
There will be a party tomorrow; Future of impersonal haber meaning there will be and always singular.
The rest is for you; Masculine noun for the rest or remainder of something.
See you tomorrow; We-form present of ver meaning we see and also see you later.
The president is speaking now; Masculine noun for a president with la presidenta used for a woman.
Where are my clothes?; Feminine noun for clothes kept singular even for a whole wardrobe.
